process_type: Atomic Layer Epitaxy (ALE) and Metalorganic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD)
summary: The study investigates the effect of hydrogen flow on indium incorporation in InGaN epitaxial films grown by atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) and metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD). It shows that reducing hydrogen flow increases the InN percentage in InGaN films, with a maximum increase of 25% when hydrogen flow is reduced from 100 to 0 sccm. The decomposition rate of ammonia is found to be less than 0.1%, indicating minimal hydrogen generation from ammonia decomposition during the process.
evidence: The InN percent in InGaN was found to be significantly influenced by the amount of hydrogen flowing into the reactor. The temperature ranges for this study are 710–780 °C for MOCVD, and 650–700 °C for ALE. For a given set of growth conditions, an increase of up to 25% InN in InGaN, as determined by x-ray diffraction, can be achieved by reducing the hydrogen flow from 100 to 0 sccm. The amount of hydrogen being generated by the ammonia at these temperatures does not appreciably change the InN percent in the films, indicating a very low decomposition rate (less than 0.1%) of the available ammonia.
